video_caption: A bald man wearing glasses and a red short-sleeved t-shirt with a grey collar stands in front of a large white board, with a microphone wire visible running down his shirt. He initially turns towards the camera, smiling slightly and giving two thumbs-up gestures, before lowering his hands and holding a white marker in his right hand. He then gestures with his right hand as he speaks. The whiteboard behind him is mostly blank, with a few faint markings near the top and left edges, and a light-colored brick wall is visible on the far left of the frame.

A man with short, thinning brown hair, wearing glasses and a red t-shirt with a dark collar, stands in front of a plain light-grey whiteboard. He holds up a printed image, which appears to be an aerial view of a complex road interchange from Google Maps, featuring a prominent circular on-ramp. He uses a white marker, which he holds in his right hand, to point at different parts of the image as he explains that it is the intersection of I12 and I59, focusing on the circular loop. He looks at the camera and asks a question about calculating a safe speed for cars on that curve before lowering the image and marker.

A man in a red t-shirt and glasses stands facing a plain white whiteboard. He is holding a white marker in his right hand, poised as if about to write or draw. He then turns his body slightly to the left, facing the whiteboard, and begins to draw a partial circle on the left side of the board. Inside the curve of the circle, he sketches a small square shape, adding a short arrow to its right, indicating movement. His gaze is directed towards the drawing as he works.

A man with short hair and glasses, wearing a red short-sleeved shirt and a watch on his left wrist, stands to the right of a whiteboard, holding a white marker in his right hand. He gestures with the marker as he speaks, looking towards the camera and occasionally up and to the right. On the whiteboard, there is a simple drawing of a circle with a small square inside, positioned on the circle's arc, and an arrow pointing in the direction of movement along the circle. The background is a plain white wall, with a faint pattern of white bricks visible on the left side.

A bald man with glasses, wearing a red short-sleeved shirt with a gray collar, stands in front of a white board, holding a black marker in his right hand and a blue marker in his left. He gestures with his right hand while talking. On the left side of the whiteboard, there's a small drawing of a circular path with a rectangular object (likely representing a car) moving along it, indicated by an arrow. Below this, the man draws a front view of a car on a flat surface. He then extends a dashed line horizontally to the right from the car, labelling the end of it with an "r". In the top right corner of the whiteboard, he writes "r = 57m" and then below it, "μs = .4", indicating the radius and coefficient of static friction, respectively. The background shows a white wall, with a grey brick wall section visible on the left.

A man wearing glasses and a red t-shirt stands in front of a whiteboard, actively drawing and explaining. On the whiteboard, he illustrates a physics problem: a circular track with a block moving along it, labeled with "r = 57m" (radius = 57 meters) and "μs = 0.4" (coefficient of static friction = 0.4). An arrow labeled "N" (normal force) points from the block towards the center of the track. Below this, he draws a car-like object on a flat surface, illustrating forces acting on it: a downward arrow labeled "mg" (gravitational force), an upward arrow labeled "N" (normal force), and a rightward arrow labeled "Ff" (friction force). He marks a horizontal dashed line as the "x" direction and gestures to indicate the vertical direction as "y". The man points to his drawings and gesticulates with his hands as he continues his explanation.

A man with short, thinning hair, wearing glasses and a red t-shirt, stands in front of a white whiteboard. He holds a white clipboard with the word "PAUSE" and three dashed lines written on it in his left hand, and a black marker in his right hand. On the whiteboard, there are physics-related drawings and text, including a circular track with a car, and another diagram resembling a multi-story structure. Textual information "r = 5.7m" (radius equals 5.7 meters) and "μs = 0.4" (coefficient of static friction equals 0.4) is visible in the top right corner. As he speaks, he gestures with his right hand towards the whiteboard, then points his index finger at the viewer, and briefly touches his temple before lowering his hand. He maintains a serious, instructional expression throughout the segment.

A man in a red short-sleeved shirt is writing on a whiteboard. On the left side of the board are hand-drawn physics diagrams, one showing an object on a curved path and another depicting a car on a flat surface with force vectors labeled 'N', 'Ff', 'mg', and 'F'. Above these diagrams, the text "r = 5.7 m" (radius = 5.7 meters) and "μs = .4" (coefficient of static friction = 0.4) is written. The man is actively writing on the right side of the whiteboard, first writing "F NET-x" (Net Force in the x-direction) followed by "F NET-y" (Net Force in the y-direction), and then starting to write "Ff =" (Friction force equals).

A man in a red short-sleeved shirt and glasses is visible from the chest up, standing in front of a whiteboard in what appears to be a classroom or office. He is holding a black marker in his right hand and actively writing on the board while explaining. On the whiteboard, there are physics diagrams and equations. In the top left, the text reads: "r = 5.7m" and "μs = .4". Below this, a diagram shows a block inside a circular path with an arrow labeled "R" pointing outwards from the block and an arrow labeled "mg" pointing downwards from the block. Below that, another diagram depicts a block on a flat surface with force arrows labeled "F_p", "F_N", and "mg". To the right, equations are written: "F_NET-x = f_s = m a_x =" where the man then adds "m v^2 / r" in real-time, and below it, "F_NET-y = N - mg = 0". The man looks towards the right side of the frame as he speaks, occasionally gesturing with the marker.

A man in a red short-sleeved shirt and glasses stands in front of a white board, which has physics diagrams and equations written on it. On the left side of the board, there is a diagram of a car moving on a circular track, with arrows indicating forces such as normal force (N), gravitational force (mg), and frictional force (F_f). Below this, there's another diagram of a car. Next to these diagrams, "r = 5.7m" and "μ_s = 0.4" are written. On the right side of the board, two equations are visible: "F_NET-x = F_f = ma_x = mv²/r" and "F_NET-y = N - mg = 0". The man points at the "mv²/r" part of the equation while speaking, then lowers his arm, and then holds up a white clipboard with the word "PAUSE" written in black capital letters and three horizontal lines below it, facing the camera. He lowers the clipboard and looks at the camera.

A man in a red t-shirt and glasses stands in front of a white board, actively explaining concepts. On the left side of the whiteboard, there's a hand-drawn diagram depicting a car on a curved road, with an arrow labeled 'N' pointing away from the road, and below it, a free-body diagram showing a normal force 'N' and gravity 'mg' pointing downwards. Above this diagram, some given values are written: "r = 57m" (radius equals 57 meters) and "μs = 0.4" (coefficient of static friction equals 0.4). On the right side of the whiteboard, equations are written: "F_{NET-x} = F_f = ma_x = mv^2/r" (Net force in x-direction equals frictional force, which equals mass times acceleration in x-direction, which also equals mass times velocity squared over radius), and "F_{NET-y} = N - mg = 0" (Net force in y-direction equals normal force minus mass times gravity, which equals zero). As he speaks about finding the frictional force, he writes the equation "f_f = μ_sN" (frictional force equals coefficient of static friction times normal force) below the existing equations. He then demonstrates deriving the normal force by writing "N - mg = 0" and "N = mg". He gestures with his right hand, pointing to various parts of the whiteboard, particularly emphasizing the newly written equations and their relation to the earlier ones. Towards the end of the clip, he holds up a small whiteboard with the word "PAUSE" and three horizontal lines written on it, indicating a moment for the viewer to pause the video and process the information.

A man in a red t-shirt and glasses stands in front of a whiteboard, actively explaining a physics problem. On the left side of the whiteboard, there's a diagram showing a car on a circular track, with arrows indicating the normal force (N) and gravitational force (mg). Below the track, a simple drawing of a building is visible. Next to the diagram, initial parameters are written: "r = 57m" (radius = 57 meters) and "μs = .4" (coefficient of static friction = 0.4). On the right side of the board, several equations are written: "F_NET-x = F_f = ma_x = mv²/r" (Net force in the x-direction is friction, mass times acceleration in x-direction, which is mass times velocity squared over radius), "F_NET-y = N - mg = 0" (Net force in the y-direction is normal force minus mass times gravity, equals zero), "f_f = μ_s N" (frictional force equals coefficient of static friction times normal force), "N - mg = 0", and "N = mg". The man uses a black marker to connect "F_f" to "mv²/r" with a curly brace, then writes "μ_s N = mv²/r" to the right. He then circles "mg" in the equation "N = mg" and draws an arrow from the circled "mg" to the "N" in "μ_s N = mv²/r", resulting in the new equation "μ_s mg = mv²/r". He then holds up a small white board with "PAUSE" written in black capital letters and gestures to the equation he just wrote on the main whiteboard, implying that viewers should pause and work on the problem.

A bald man wearing a red short-sleeved t-shirt stands in front of a whiteboard, explaining physics concepts. On the left side of the whiteboard, there are two hand-drawn diagrams: one depicts a car on a circular track with labels "r = 57m" and "μs = 0.4", and another shows a car on a flat surface with forces "F", "N", and "mg" indicated by arrows. On the right side, the man has written a series of equations: "F_NET-X = F_f = ma_x = m v^2 / r", "F_NET-Y = N - mg = 0", "F_f = μ_s N", with arrows showing how these equations combine to derive "μ_s N = m v^2 / r" and "N = (mg)", ultimately leading to "μ_s mg = m v^2 / r". The man then uses a black marker to further simplify this, writing "V^2 = μ_s g r" and "V = √(μ_s g r)", circling the expression "μ_s g r" under the square root. He gestures with his hands as he speaks, then turns to the board to begin substituting numerical values into the derived formula, writing "V = √((.4)(9.8m/s^2)(57m))".

A bald man wearing a red t-shirt stands in front of a whiteboard in a classroom setting, actively explaining a physics problem. The whiteboard is filled with handwritten calculations, diagrams, and equations related to centripetal force and friction. On the top left, parameters `r = 57M` (radius = 57 meters) and `Ms = .4` (coefficient of static friction = 0.4) are visible. Two diagrams illustrate a car: one from a top-down perspective on a circular track with normal force (N) and friction force (Fr) vectors, and another from a side view showing normal force (N) and gravitational force (mg) vectors. The derivations on the right side of the board show `F_NET-X = f_s = ma_x = m v^2 / r` and `F_NET-Y = N - mg = 0`. Further steps lead to `f_s = μ_s N`, `N = mg`, and ultimately `V = sqrt(μ_s g r)`. The man performs a calculation, writing `V = sqrt((0.4)(9.8 m/s^2)(57 m))` which yields `15 m/s`. He then converts this to `34 mph`. While gesturing with his hands, he explains the practical application of the calculation, suggesting a safe speed limit by writing and underlining `25 mph` on the whiteboard. He looks at the camera, smiles, and briefly gives a thumbs-up before turning away.
